themes.name: Critical Thinking Enhancement through AI
themes.definition: AI tools, such as chatbots and large language models, are designed or used to foster and improve students' critical thinking skills by encouraging reflection, exploration of multiple perspectives, and deeper cognitive engagement.
evidence: [Favero2025] the proposed Socratic tutor encourages students to explore various perspectives and engage in self-reflection
[Lee2025a] GPT-CMDP students had significantly higher academic performance and better critical thinking and problem-solving skills
[Tashtoush2025] significant improvements in the mean scores of critical thinking skills among secondary students who were exposed to Artificial Intelligence Techniques

themes.name: Development of Higher-Order Thinking Skills through AI
themes.definition: AI integration in educational contexts aims to enhance a range of higher-order thinking skills, including critical thinking, creative thinking, problem-solving, and reflective thinking.
evidence: [Waziana2025] the ChatGPT group achieved statistically significant gains in critical, creative, and reflective thinking scores
[Lin2025c] enhance English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners’ writing performance and higher-order thinking skills
[Kabeer2025] significant advancements in creativity, imagination, and critical thinking

themes.name: Personalized and Adaptive AI in Education
themes.definition: AI systems provide customized learning experiences through personalized feedback, adaptive learning pathways, and content adaptation based on individual learner data.
evidence: [Kumar2025] the paper proposes an AI-based framework of customizing the creative learning trajectory
[Kurniawan2025a] personalized feedback, adaptive learning pathways, and real-time analytics
[Vertemati2024] an intelligent tutoring system that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to personalize learning

themes.name: Ethical and Critical Engagement with AI
themes.definition: Addressing the challenges of uncritical reliance on AI, with a focus on developing strategies for ethical use, academic integrity, and critical evaluation of AI-generated outputs.
evidence: [Cong-Lem2026] developing critical, strategic, and ethical engagement with ChatGPT
[Anwar2025] use it ethically, appropriately, and responsibly in their studies
[Kim2025] promoting awareness of the ethical implications of AI

themes.name: AI Applications in Specific Educational Domains
themes.definition: The application of AI tools in particular academic subjects or fields, such as nursing, chemistry, mathematics, and language learning, to enhance domain-specific knowledge and skills.
evidence: [Karaçay2025] nursing students' experiences towards using ChatGPT as a teaching tool
[Kim2025] integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chatbots and Green Chemistry Principles
[Alshehri2025] integrating Automated Writing Evaluation into Saudi EFL Students' Writing Practice

themes.name: Teacher Support and Human Guidance in AI-Integrated Education
themes.definition: Emphasizing the continued importance of human educators in providing contextual guidance, ethical oversight, and instructional support alongside AI tools.
evidence: [Hönigsberg2025] underscoring the continued importance of human educators in providing critical, ethical, and contextual guidance
[Fang2026] teacher support significantly influences student engagement and learning outcomes
[Yongzhi2024] require a high degree of preparatory work and active student management by the teacher

themes.name: Cognitive Effects of AI Dependence
themes.definition: Exploring how reliance on AI tools affects cognitive load, fatigue, and thinking skills, with insights into managing these impacts through literacy and support.
evidence: [Tian2025] greater AI dependence was associated with lower levels of critical thinking, with cognitive fatigue partially mediating this relationship
[Yuxian2025] critical thinking guidance fosters procedural learning but increases cognitive load
[Waziana2025] expressed concerns about risks such as cognitive offloading and skill atrophy

data.meta_observations: Common methodological approaches in the abstracts include quasi-experimental designs, case studies, and mixed-methods research, often focused on higher education or specific student groups. There is a trend towards evaluating AI tools in real educational settings, with an emphasis on skill enhancement and ethical considerations.
data.grounding_notes: Evidence is based solely on explicit statements from the abstracts, as some have quality notes indicating missing elements (e.g., no quantitative data, missing methods). Quotes are verbatim where available; no inference is made beyond what is stated. All article keys are from the provided closed set.
